rationale: Thresholds for BMS per-session diagnostics, computed directly from real per-cell/pack telemetry in a 'processed_data' export. These are conventional EV-BMS engineering rules of thumb (cited below), not fitted to this specific pack's real failure outcomes -- no failure-labelled data exists yet for this vehicle. Revisit once real fault/replacement history is available.
cell_imbalance_rationale: 0.03-0.05V sustained pack-level cell imbalance is a commonly cited threshold in EV BMS literature for when active cell balancing should be reviewed; below this, small imbalances are normal manufacturing/aging variation.
soc_disagreement_rationale: SoC-EKF and SoC-Coulomb-Count are two independent state-of-charge estimators already computed in this data. They should track closely; a sustained gap indicates one estimator (usually Coulomb counting, which drifts without periodic recalibration) has lost accuracy. 3-6% is a conservative band given normal estimator jitter.
thermal_spread_rationale: Spread across the pack's 3 cell-temperature sensors during a single session. Meaningful spread suggests uneven cooling/airflow or a developing hotspot; single-digit-C spread is normal in most air/passively-cooled packs.
trend_rationale: State-space (Kalman) trend over Pack SoH across sessions, reusing the same StateSpaceModel already used for OBD degradation trends. Revision history: the first calibration (process_noise_var_soh=0.3, velocity=0.0001, threshold=0.05%/day) was tuned only against this dataset's own dense, ~2-month, near-daily session cadence -- a 500-trial Monte Carlo check (synthetic sessions spanning a realistic 1-year, ~weekly cadence, with the same ~1pp session-to-session wobble this dataset shows) found two problems: (1) at realistic multi-week gaps between sessions the old noise parameters let a single noisy point whipsaw the velocity estimate, flagging WORSENING on pure noise as often as on real injected degradation; (2) threshold=0.05%/day equals 18%/year, which real Li-ion packs would only reach via near-total failure, not the 1.5-3%/year literature range for normal aging -- meaning the old config could never have flagged realistic gradual degradation as WORSENING even if the pipeline saw it. Current values were chosen by the same Monte Carlo sweep: process_noise_var_soh=0.02 and velocity=2e-7 keep the filter responsive without whipsawing on isolated noisy points at multi-week gaps; direction_threshold_pct_per_day=0.006 (~2.2%/year) sits between the noise-only false-positive rate (~18% at this threshold) and reliable detection of faster-than-normal decline (~66% true-positive at 3%/year decline in a 1-year window). Detecting mild, normal-range decline (~1.5%/year) within under a year of data remains statistically weak (~30-40% true-positive) -- this is a genuine signal-to-noise limit of point-to-point session readings, not something a threshold alone fixes, which is why session aggregation was added (see trend_aggregation_window_sessions) and why the report surfaces the model's own uncertainty rather than a bare label. All of this is provisional pending real longitudinal packs with confirmed fade outcomes, exactly like every other model in this codebase.
trend_aggregation_rationale: Before the Kalman filter runs, consecutive sessions are grouped into buckets of this size (averaging SoH, confidence, and elapsed time within each bucket) to reduce per-session estimator noise the same way averaging reduces any i.i.d. noise: roughly by sqrt(window). A discontinuity (pack swap/recalibration) always starts a new bucket rather than being smoothed across. The Monte Carlo sweep above found window=5 cut the noise-only slope estimate's standard deviation from ~0.024%/day (no aggregation) to ~0.006%/day, without needing more real sessions than this dataset already has.
